newsitem.title: UK: LME copper down in volatile trade, others follow.
newsitem.headline: LME copper down in volatile trade, others follow.

text.p: The copper market's steep backwardation contracted slightly on Tuesday afternoon, and prices responded by sliding below $2,300 a tonne in whipsaw trading, dealers said.
Copper's choppy behaviour was reflected throughout the base metals complex, with most London Metal Exchange (LME) metals ending the afternoon kerb in the minus column.
Flagship three months copper came off an early high of $2,337 to finish just above the day's lows at $2,278, compared to Monday's kerb close of $2,315.
The cash to threes backwardation, which flared by $100 during Third Wednesday pricing on Monday, ended the kerb little changed at $250/$255.
However, it narrowed from the $270 high attained in the first ring, when the tomorrow/next trading surged to a $24 backwardation -- just $1 short of the LME limit.
But traders expected tightness to persist over the next two weeks.
"Trading is going to be whippy and volatile with a backwardation like this," a trader said.
Another noted that shorts had elected to roll positions forward rather than cover outright.
One trader added that as a result of the backwardation, some 50,000 tonnes of copper was expected to enter LME warehouses in the coming weeks, particularly Singapore and the U.S.
LME stocks rose by a modest 2,100 tonnes in the morning.
The other metals were generally weaker with copper.
"They're all looking sorrowful, taking the lead from copper. Once copper turned lower there was no stopping the other metals," a trader said.
Zinc ended in the middle of the day's range, failing to recover back above the $1,500 level it achieved on Monday. It ended the kerb at $1,491, down $11.
Aluminium was also lower and dealers noted that trading was made difficult by uncertainty in copper.
Kerb trading ended $21 lower at $1,563 per tonne.

Lead sustained a major drop, tumbling $20 to $638 after making strong upside progress earlier this month. Below $650 it hit sell stops, traders noted, but then it found some support at its 30-day moving average around $636.
Tin followed the others down $75 to $5,515 and alloy was off sharply at $1,415/$1,425, compared with $1,435/1,440.
Below $1,415, alloy prices would enter fresh low territory for the year.
